text:
maya: Quick question — we're seeing streaming responses get cut off sometimes when Polly retries happen. Using IHttpClientFactory (AddHttpClient("llm")), and I call `client.GetAsync(url, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead)` then `var stream = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync()` and pipe that to a consumer. Occasionally the stream ends mid-payload when a retry runs. Any pointers?

kevin: Are you sure you're not disposing the HttpResponseMessage or HttpClient too early? Common pattern is `using var resp = ...` then `using var stream = ...` — if the outer scope disposes before the consumer finishes you'll see truncation.

maya: Example snippet I'm using: `using var resp = await client.GetAsync(url, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead); using var stream = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(); await stream.CopyToAsync(destStream);` I thought ResponseHeadersRead prevents buffering — could Polly retry be interfering?

sam: ResponseHeadersRead is correct to avoid buffering, but retries can cause troubles if the retry policy wraps the whole method that also owns disposal. If the handler retries at the HTTP handler level it's fine, but if your code calls GetAsync multiple times (via policy.ExecuteAsync) you might be abandoning a previous resp/stream. Also check how timeouts/cancellation tokens are wired between Polly and HttpClient.

olga: Another gotcha: register the retry policy as part of the HttpClient pipeline (AddPolicyHandler) so the request is retried inside the handler stack rather than by re-executing your higher-level code which may recreate request/response objects. e.g. `services.AddHttpClient("llm").AddPolicyHandler(retryPolicy)`

maya: We're doing `AddHttpClient("llm").AddPolicyHandler(retryPolicy)`, but in some places we still wrap calls in a local retry because we need per-request retry counts. Could that be the culprit?

kevin: If you wrap the whole method in a retry, each attempt will create a new HttpRequestMessage/response lifecycle. That can be fine but you must ensure previous response/stream is fully disposed only after the consumer is done. Prefer letting the handler-level policy do transport retries. If you need dynamic behavior, consider a delegating handler that reads context or use named clients for different policies.

sam: Operational tips: set `MaxConnectionsPerServer` on your SocketsHttpHandler (via AddHttpMessageHandler or configure primary handler) and tune `PooledConnectionLifetime` if your load balancer recycles upstream connections. Also avoid `ReadAsStringAsync()` — it buffers. Use streams and `ResponseHeadersRead`.

olga: Also check you aren't hitting `HttpClient.Timeout` prematurely; if you want per-try timeouts use Polly's `TimeoutPolicy` so cancellation comes through the handler pipeline correctly and you don't abort the underlying socket unexpectedly.

infra-bot: FYI I added a lint check to the repo: PRs that create `new HttpClient()` will get a warning and we now have a checklist item to prefer AddHttpClient and AddPolicyHandler. See https://redwood.dev/prs/1234

maya: Thanks — I'll refactor to rely on AddPolicyHandler/delegating handler pattern and stop doing method-level retries for this flow. I'll also double-check disposal scopes so the response isn't disposed before the consumer finishes. Will post a PR shortly.

devx-bot: @maya quick reminder: add a lightweight integration test that simulates partial stream cancellation (we have helpers in devex/test-utils) so we don't regress.

maya: Will do — pinging reviewers when ready. Thanks everyone!
